text:
ROXANE:
  Let me have your hand—come now, it has a fever.—
  But I saw the confession trembling on his lips.

CYRANO:
  Ah!...

ROXANE (finishing a little bandage for him with her handkerchief):
  And just imagine—why, as it happens,
  Yes, cousin, he serves in your regiment!

CYRANO:
  Ah!...

ROXANE (laughing):
  For he is a cadet in your company!

CYRANO:
  Ah!...

ROXANE:
  His brow bespeaks wit and genius;
  He is proud, noble, young, intrepid, handsome...

CYRANO (rising, deathly pale):
  Handsome!

ROXANE:
  What? What is the matter with you?

CYRANO:
  Nothing... It is... it is...
  (He points to his hand, with a smile):
  It is this little hurt.

ROXANE:
  In short, I love him. Besides, I must tell you
  That I have never seen him except at the theater...

CYRANO:
  So you have not spoken to each other?

ROXANE:
  Only our eyes have.

CYRANO:
  But then how do you know?

ROXANE:
  Beneath the lindens
  Of the Place Royale, people talk... Some gossips
  Informed me...

CYRANO:
  He is a cadet?

ROXANE:
  A cadet in the Guards.

CYRANO:
  His name?

ROXANE:
  Baron Christian de Neuvillette.

CYRANO:
  What?...
  He is not in the Cadets.

ROXANE:
  Yes, since this morning:
  Captain Carbon de Castel-Jaloux.

CYRANO:
  How swiftly,
  How swiftly one gives away one’s heart!... But, my poor little one...

THE DUENNA (opening the door at the back):
  I have finished the cakes, Monsieur de Bergerac!

CYRANO:
  Well, then! Read the verses printed on the bag!
  (The duenna disappears):
  ...My poor child, you who love only fine language
  And brilliant wit—what if he were a philistine, a savage?

ROXANE:
  No, he has the hair of one of d’Urfé’s heroes!

CYRANO:
  What if his speech were as foul as his hair is fine!

ROXANE:
  No, every word he says is refined—I can tell!

CYRANO:
  Yes, every word is refined when the mustache is fine.
  —But what if he were a fool!...

ROXANE (stamping her foot):
  Well then, I would die of it, there and then!

CYRANO (after a pause):
  You asked me to come so that you could tell me this?
  I do not quite see the point of it, madame.

ROXANE:
  Ah, it is because yesterday someone filled my soul with mortal dread
  By telling me that all of you, all of you are Gascons
  In your company...

CYRANO:
  And that we challenge
  Every beardless boy who, through favor, gains admittance
  Among the pure Gascons we are, without being one himself?
  Is that what you were told?

ROXANE:
  And you can imagine how I
  Trembled for him!

CYRANO (between his teeth):
  Not without reason!

ROXANE:
  But I thought,
  When yesterday you appeared before us, invincible and great,
  Punishing that scoundrel, standing up to those brutes—
  I thought: if he were willing, he whom they will all fear...

CYRANO:
  Very well, I shall protect your little baron.

ROXANE:
  Oh! You will protect him for me, will you not?
  I have always felt such tender friendship for you.

CYRANO:
  Yes, yes.

ROXANE:
  You will be his friend?

CYRANO:
  I shall.

ROXANE:
  And he will never have to fight a duel?

CYRANO:
  I swear it.

ROXANE:
  Oh! I am very fond of you. I must be going.
  (She quickly puts her mask back on, arranges a lace veil over her brow, and,
  distractedly):
  But you have not told me about the battle
  Last night. Truly, it must have been extraordinary!...
  —Tell him to write to me.
  (She blows him a little kiss from her hand):
  Oh! I love you!

CYRANO:
  Yes, yes.

ROXANE:
  A hundred men against you? Come, farewell.—We are
  Great friends!

CYRANO:
  Yes, yes.

ROXANE:
  Have him write to me!—A hundred men!—
  You will tell me later. I cannot now.
  A hundred men! What courage!

CYRANO (bowing to her):
  Oh! I have done better since then.
  (She exits. Cyrano remains motionless, his eyes on the ground. A silence. The
  door on the right opens. Ragueneau puts his head through.)



Scene 2.VII.

Cyrano, Ragueneau, the poets, Carbon de Castel-Jaloux, the cadets, the
crowd, etc., then De Guiche.


RAGUENEAU:
  May we come back in?

CYRANO (without moving):
  Yes...
  (Ragueneau signals, and his friends come back in. At the same time, Carbon
  de Castel-Jaloux appears at the door at the back, dressed as a captain in
  the Guards, making broad gestures when he catches sight of Cyrano.)

CARBON DE CASTEL-JALOUX:
  There he is!

CYRANO (raising his head):
  My captain!...

CARBON (exultantly):
  Our hero! We know everything! Some thirty
  Of my cadets are here!...

CYRANO (drawing back):
  But...

CARBON (trying to pull him along):
  Come! They want to see you!

CYRANO:
  No!

CARBON:
  They are drinking across the way, at the Croix du Trahoir.

CYRANO:
  I...

CARBON (going up to the door and shouting into the wings in a voice of
  thunder):
  The hero refuses. He is in a surly mood!

A VOICE (outside):
  God’s blood!
  (Commotion outside, the sound of swords and boots drawing nearer.)

CARBON (rubbing his hands):
  Here they come, crossing the street!

THE CADETS (entering the pastry shop):
  A thousand gods!—God’s head!—God’s death!—By God’s little head!

RAGUENEAU (drawing back in terror):
  Gentlemen, are you all from Gascony, then?

THE CADETS:
  All of us!

A CADET (to Cyrano):
  Bravo!

CYRANO:
  Baron!

ANOTHER (shaking his hands):
  Long live Cyrano!

CYRANO:
  Baron!

THIRD CADET:
  Let me embrace you!

CYRANO:
  Baron!...

SEVERAL GASCONS:
  Let us embrace him!

CYRANO (not knowing which one to answer):
  Baron!... Baron!... Please...

RAGUENEAU:
  Are you all barons, gentlemen?

THE CADETS:
  All?

RAGUENEAU:
  Are they?...

FIRST CADET:
  One could build a tower from our coronets alone!

LE BRET (entering and running to Cyrano):
  They are looking for you! A delirious crowd, led
  By those who followed behind you last night...

CYRANO (horrified):
  You did not tell them where I am?...

LE BRET (rubbing his hands):
  I did!

A BURGHER (entering, followed by a group):
  Monsieur, the whole Marais is having itself carried here!
  (Outside, the street has filled with people. Sedan chairs and carriages
  draw to a halt.)

LE BRET (softly, smiling, to Cyrano):
  And Roxane?

CYRANO (sharply):
  Be quiet!

THE CROWD (shouting outside):
  Cyrano!...
  (A mob rushes into the pastry shop. Jostling. Cheers.)
